# K-M.1 — All-to-all MoE inventory and pins

Source inspection: **2026-11-12**, launch/helper supplement **2026-11-13** ([#425](https://github.com/dnyBLUESKY007/VeriTile/issues/425)). This is the document-only inventory for [#180](https://github.com/dnyBLUESKY007/VeriTile/issues/180), using [K-D.1 / #166](https://github.com/dnyBLUESKY007/VeriTile/issues/166)'s acceptance: functions per file, primitives, launch shapes and pins. The [map (#1)](https://github.com/dnyBLUESKY007/VeriTile/issues/1) owns the versions; the K-M rows of [`scripts/census/targets.tsv`](../../scripts/census/targets.tsv) own the enumerated source targets. The original manifest and scanner were read at VeriTile `a0ba977236322702b1d0d8b891a34a4e1c9b2074`; the supplement used the scanner at `8ed0f696dd2cf91c71c76a6a45fa8b05081350fe`.

**35 Triton-distributed + 2 TileLang = 37 rows**, covering every decorated function recognized by the scanner in these eight files. D7's nested `calc_gather_index._kernel` is included. The TileScale pin also contains [the same fused-MoE file](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilescale/blob/71e71457d40ed6e6a2dad297936bfdbff21d104b/examples/fusedmoe/example_fusedmoe_tilelang.py); both files have Git blob `a8c78c7674b78a6589daf1c90b6c99dca4c61792`. It therefore shares L1's two rows and four launch regions, but is not an additional K-M target in the manifest. This byte equality does not establish equality of their frameworks or runtimes.

The six TileScale port entries have blank source paths in the pinned manifest. They have no source body to census in this target set; a missing target path is not a scan proving that no related code exists anywhere in the repository.

## Per-function census: observed calls

The real [`scripts/census/scan.py`](../../scripts/census/scan.py) CLI parses Python ASTs without importing or running the target. Every row below is marked `kernel: true` by that scanner, including decorated device helpers; this flag does **not** mean an independent host launch. No additional undecorated reachable same-file helper rows were emitted. Decorator aliases are resolved by the scanner. `jit` below means `triton.jit`, `dist.jit` means `triton_dist.jit`, and `tile.jit` means `tilelang.jit`.

The call column lists **all distinct normalized call names**, with multiple signatures collapsed to their total syntactic call-site count (`×N`). Counts are static occurrences, not runtime invocation counts. Prefix abbreviations: `tl` = `triton.language`; `td` = `triton_dist.language`; `T` = `tilelang.language`; `cuda` = `triton_dist.language.extra.cuda.language_extra`; `extra` = `triton_dist.language.extra.language_extra`; `shmem` = `triton_dist.language.extra.libshmem_device`; `common` = `triton_dist.kernels.nvidia.common_ops`; `kernels` = `triton_dist.kernels.nvidia`; `profiler` = `triton_dist.tools.profiler`. Bare names are built-ins or same-file helpers. Leading-dot names (such as `.to`, `.load`, `.record`) are receiver calls whose receiver the scanner leaves unresolved. Names such as `cuda.ld` describe the exposed Python API only; no lower-level instruction contract is inferred.

This is a call inventory, not the complete operator/type inventory: operators, subscripts, attribute-only constants, imported helper bodies, decorator configuration and most host code are outside this call column. Imported calls remain visible as boundaries. Same-file decorated helper bodies have their own rows.

## Launch shapes: separate source inspection

All shapes below come from same-file host launch expressions or TileLang `T.Kernel` regions; they were not inferred from the scanner's `kernel` flag. `cdiv`/`ceildiv` denote the source's ceiling-division helpers; `SM_count` is the queried device `multi_processor_count`, not a measured constant. `BM`, `BN`, `BK` abbreviate `BLOCK_SIZE_M/N/K`. Additional configuration evidence:

- D4's [default configuration helper](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Triton-distributed/blob/7908e4ea9010bb2238f9f05b28c904fd4b71c60a/python/triton_dist/kernels/nvidia/moe_reduce_rs.py#L795) sets BN=128, BK=64, eight warps and three stages; persistent BM=128, nonpersistent BM=64 because the [loop at L805–808](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Triton-distributed/blob/7908e4ea9010bb2238f9f05b28c904fd4b71c60a/python/triton_dist/kernels/nvidia/moe_reduce_rs.py#L805-L808) iterates `[128, 64]` without a break and assigns the final loop variable after the loop (for inputs reaching that assignment). D5's [default helper](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Triton-distributed/blob/7908e4ea9010bb2238f9f05b28c904fd4b71c60a/python/triton_dist/kernels/nvidia/moe_reduce_ar.py#L200) sets BM/BN/BK=128/128/64, eight warps and three stages. Both compute GROUP_SIZE_N from N_per_chunk. These defaults do not override an explicitly supplied `config`.
- D6's [context defaults](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Triton-distributed/blob/7908e4ea9010bb2238f9f05b28c904fd4b71c60a/python/triton_dist/kernels/nvidia/allgather_group_gemm.py#L291) are BM/BN/BK=128/256/64, GROUP_SIZE_M=8, three stages and eight warps; the consumer launch reads the context fields. Its [imported swizzle launch](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Triton-distributed/blob/7908e4ea9010bb2238f9f05b28c904fd4b71c60a/python/triton_dist/kernels/nvidia/allgather_group_gemm.py#L235) calls `threadblock_swizzle_ag_moe_kernel[(1,)]`, with `num_warps=swizzle_num_warps`. That imported function is counted separately above, outside the eight target files.
- D7's [decorator](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Triton-distributed/blob/7908e4ea9010bb2238f9f05b28c904fd4b71c60a/tutorials/04-deepseek-infer-all2all.py#L89) supplies the single BM=16 / 16-warp autotune configuration. Its [host kwargs](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Triton-distributed/blob/7908e4ea9010bb2238f9f05b28c904fd4b71c60a/tutorials/04-deepseek-infer-all2all.py#L538) set world size, hidden width, token capacity, expert count and optional online FP8 quantization. The two dispatch/combine launches share the grid but use different MODE values and buffer roles. The quant/dequant host calls do not explicitly specify warp counts; none is guessed here.
- Both L1 eager functions default block_token/block_dhidden/block_dexpert to 128, threads to 256 and num_stages to 1 ([shared signature](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/35850c06875bcc84751417982bf7b4d662bafdbc/examples/fusedmoe/example_fusedmoe_tilelang.py#L12), [routed signature](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/35850c06875bcc84751417982bf7b4d662bafdbc/examples/fusedmoe/example_fusedmoe_tilelang.py#L92)). Their decorators disable warp specialization. These are configurable source defaults, not an observed runtime selection. The routed launch uses the actual [M assignment](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/35850c06875bcc84751417982bf7b4d662bafdbc/examples/fusedmoe/example_fusedmoe_tilelang.py#L120), `ceil(group_sum/block_token)+group_count`, rather than the alternative formula in the preceding comment.

## Rank and host launch shape

The shared launcher (**S**) uses `torchrun`, takes an explicit `--nproc_per_node=N` override (otherwise `ARNOLD_WORKER_GPU` or the `nvidia-smi` device count), and takes `nnodes=ARNOLD_WORKER_NUM` (default 1): [scripts/launch.sh L146–173](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Triton-distributed/blob/7908e4ea9010bb2238f9f05b28c904fd4b71c60a/scripts/launch.sh#L146-L173). Its [option parser](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Triton-distributed/blob/7908e4ea9010bb2238f9f05b28c904fd4b71c60a/scripts/launch.sh#L3-L16) accepts that override among the launcher arguments. The shared initialization (**I**) reads `RANK`, `WORLD_SIZE`, `LOCAL_RANK` and `LOCAL_WORLD_SIZE`, binds `torch.cuda.set_device(LOCAL_RANK)`, and creates the group: [utils.py L339–355](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Triton-distributed/blob/7908e4ea9010bb2238f9f05b28c904fd4b71c60a/python/triton_dist/utils.py#L339-L355). Thus the source launcher assigns one process to each local GPU index; it does not itself enforce this project's two-GPU request cap. For the one-host/two-process shape use the existing launcher override with `ARNOLD_WORKER_NUM=1`; merely setting visible devices is not evidence that the launcher's fallback device count is capped.

The final column is a **source-level rank/launch-shape assessment**, not hardware acceptance: “yes” means the stated assertions permit that shape with the cited test inputs. H800 compilation, memory capacity, connectivity, peer atomic support and execution are unchecked for every row. Project limits and logical-node requirements are in [GpuInterNodeRuns](../GpuInterNodeRuns.md). A missing command means no command for that target was found in the bounded [docs/testing.md](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Triton-distributed/blob/7908e4ea9010bb2238f9f05b28c904fd4b71c60a/docs/testing.md#L1-L282) inspection, not that no runnable test exists.

## Interpretation and boundaries

**Inference for follow-on work:** D1–D3 separate split/offset handling, data movement and barriers; D4/D5 pair grouped GEMM variants with reduction/communication kernels; D6 combines gather-index construction, copy/reset/barrier preparation and GEMM consumers; D7 demonstrates dispatch/combine with optional quantization; L1 contains shared and routed expert arithmetic in two stages each. This grouping follows the observed call sites and launch structure above. It is not a correctness theorem, a guarantee about synchronization, or a performance result.

**Unchecked:** external source compilation/execution, actual grids on hardware, supported topology, allocation/stream ordering across the complete application, framework defaults not explicitly supplied, imported helper runtime behavior, generated code, numeric equivalence, termination/race freedom, and any new numerical or memory-order assumption. No GPU execution or Lean change is required or claimed by this document-only ticket. The six missing TileScale targets remain unimplemented in this inventory, and D6's two unlaunched persistent variants remain without a same-file launch shape.

## Reproduction and validation

Use read-only scratch checkouts at the pins above. Set `VERITILE_ROOT`, `TD_SOURCE` and `TL_SOURCE` to their checkout roots. Run the repository-owned scanner, not any external Python module:

```sh
(cd "$TD_SOURCE" && python3 "$VERITILE_ROOT/scripts/census/scan.py" \
  python/triton_dist/kernels/nvidia/all_to_all_single_2d.py \
  python/triton_dist/kernels/nvidia/all_to_all_vdev_2d_offset.py \
  python/triton_dist/kernels/nvidia/all_to_all_vdev_2d_offset_inter_node.py \
  python/triton_dist/kernels/nvidia/moe_reduce_rs.py \
  python/triton_dist/kernels/nvidia/moe_reduce_ar.py \
  python/triton_dist/kernels/nvidia/allgather_group_gemm.py \
  tutorials/04-deepseek-infer-all2all.py)
(cd "$TL_SOURCE" && python3 "$VERITILE_ROOT/scripts/census/scan.py" \
  examples/fusedmoe/example_fusedmoe_tilelang.py)
(cd "$TD_SOURCE" && python3 "$VERITILE_ROOT/scripts/census/scan.py" \
  python/triton_dist/kernels/nvidia/gemm_rs_threadblock_swizzle.py \
  python/triton_dist/kernels/nvidia/moe_utils.py \
  python/triton_dist/kernels/nvidia/threadblock_swizzle_ag_moe_triton.py)
```

The helper scanner command also exited 0 (16 records emitted; three selected above); the three selected records match its definition lines, decorators and aggregated normalized call counts.
